\[
\begin{gathered}
\begin{bmatrix} R' \\ G' \\ B' \end{bmatrix} =
\begin{bmatrix}
0.393 + 0.607 k & 0.769 - 0.769 k & 0.189 - 0.189 k \\
0.349 - 0.349 k & 0.686 + 0.314 k & 0.168 - 0.168 k \\
0.272 - 0.272 k & 0.534 - 0.534 k & 0.131 + 0.869 k
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} R \\ G \\ B \end{bmatrix},
\qquad k = 1 - \frac{ 100 }{100}
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(R, G, B\): The encoded channel values from 0 to 255
- \(k\): One minus the amount, from 0 to 1

This is the matrix of the CSS sepia() function in the W3C Filter Effects spec. With k = 0 it is the full sepia matrix. Its rows add up to more than 1 for red and green and less than 1 for blue, so white turns cream and gray turns brown. With k = 1 it is the identity. The matrix acts on the encoded sRGB values from 0 to 255, and the results are clipped to 0 to 255.
